attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He states the point in his own voice and is not quoting anyone.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense observation. The context is about lawyers, while the normalised claim covers all legal filings, which is slightly broader. That does not matter here, because most of the May 2025 cases involved legal professionals.

contract.note: Using May 2025 as the period follows from his 'just this month'. Reading 'routine' as several court findings a week across different courts is an ordinary plain reading. Any reasonable threshold gives the same result.

evidence.note: Business Insider, May 27, 2025, citing Charlotin's data: at least 23 judicial call-outs since May 1. That is about five or six a week.

The same report: legal professionals were at fault in at least 13 of the 23 recent cases, which fits the focus on lawyers. The 'last month' wording is slightly ambiguous, but it matches the May count.
A dated May 6, 2025 sanctions order against two large law firms for AI-fabricated research. It is one confirmed instance within the target month.
Charlotin's description in October 2025 of the rate before and after spring 2025. It is a retrospective view, not a count for May, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: Court findings of AI-fabricated citations in May 2025 numbered at least 23 in under four weeks, across different courts and filers, and most involved lawyers. That meets the contract's support condition of many independent findings a week. The packet contains no counterevidence showing only isolated cases. The count comes from Business Insider's reading of Charlotin's database rather than a direct count, but it is consistent and from a reputable source.
